==English==

===Pronunciation===
* {{audio|en|en-au-hand over.ogg|a=AU}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb|*}}

# {{lb|en|transitive|idiomatic}} To [[relinquish]] [[control]] or [[possession]] of something to someone.
#: {{ux|en|I '''handed over''' the controls to the copilot.}}
#* {{RQ:en:New York Times
|date=July 14, 2013
|author=Joyce Lau; Calvin Yang
|title=University of Macau Moves Over the China Border
|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130718100329/https://www.nytimes.com/2013/07/15/world/asia/University-of-Macau-Moves-Over-the-China-Border.html
|archivedate=18 July 2013
|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2013/07/15/world/asia/University-of-Macau-Moves-Over-the-China-Border.html
|section=Asia Pacific
|text=When classes start in September, the University of Macau’s new campus — still under construction on about a square kilometer, or roughly 250 acres, on Hengqin Island in southern Guangdong Province — will be “'''handed over'''” to Macau governance in accordance with a 2009 bill by the National People’s Congress in Beijing.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|idiomatic}} To [[deliver]] (someone to an enemy, police, etc.).
